rulings.challenge_claim: Two items. Raised by both challenges: the front-seam warrant at Jer.48.9 is a plural imperative with no named vocative addressee - the same shape the unit closing at Jer.48.8 refused as a seam at Jer.48.6 on exactly that no-named-vocative ground - and the row reconciles the two nowhere, no other tier-1 or tier-3 signal falling at the seam. Raised by one challenge: the singleness asserted for the slackness noun at Jer.48.10 is stated in words only, with neither of the two digits that would make the point.
rulings.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects on one row, not one defect twice. Item 1 (raised by both), the front-seam parity objection: byte-true as far as it goes. oshb:Jer.48.9 opens תְּנוּ (byte), a plural imperative, with Moab standing in the lamed phrase לְמוֹאָ֔ב (oshb:Jer.48.9, byte) and a third-person suffix on her cities, so no vocative addressee is named; oshb:Jer.48.6 opens נֻ֖סוּ מַלְּט֣וּ (byte), likewise plural imperatives with a second-person plural suffix and no vocative. Correction to the objection's evidence: Moab is not named at all in oshb:Jer.48.6, so the two verses are not parallel in the way one challenge states them; the genuinely shared feature is the absent vocative, not third-person reference to Moab. The only differentiator the row offers is a change of figure (wings against flight on foot), which is texture rather than a device class, so the warrant as written would license a cut at oshb:Jer.48.6 just as well. That is the real defect, and it is a warrant-and-disclosure defect, not evidence that the span is wrong. NEW FINDING, undisclosed by the row and by both challenges: oshb:Jer.48.8 closes verse-final on אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.8, byte), a three-token relative-clause divine speech attribution standing in exactly one verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, contiguous token sequence, skeleton tier) - a speech-formula-class closure signal on the near side of the seam, which under the ruled ordering corroborates a close wherever a fresh onset follows, as the imperative at oshb:Jer.48.9 does. No comparable attribution stands before oshb:Jer.48.6, which is exactly the distinction the row fails to draw. Seam environment re-derived: within Jer 48 the messenger formula stands only at oshb:Jer.48.1 and oshb:Jer.48.40 (sweep: 2 verses, koh-amar bigram, skeleton tier), the chapter's only inventoried woe site and its only nation header both sit at oshb:Jer.48.1 (1 site each, this chapter), and the sole parashah mark anywhere in oshb:Jer.48.1-Jer.48.30 is the setumah at oshb:Jer.48.11 (1 mark) (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets) - so the negative half of the objection verifies. Item 2 (raised by one challenge), the undigited exclusivity: upheld outright. The row asserts the slackness noun רְמִיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.48.10, byte) is 'the single attested token at this one site' and appeals to 'every occurrence of the prophet's own name', with no digit anywhere in the field. The digits exist and are exact: whole-token equality returns 1 verse at byte and at skeleton tier (oshb:Jer.48.10); the bare consonantal substring returns 118 verses and 132 token occurrences, because the prophet's name carries that skeleton. An exclusivity claim is never tier-dampened, so the byte label on the splice does not cover it. NEW FINDING on the declared-flag queue for this row: the three universals flags split - the one landing on the singleness sentence marks a real defect, while the two 'never' flags (never as a book-wide count; never generalized into a count) are self-scoped statements about the row's own practice and are genuine false positives that need no edit. Severity held at medium: a front-seam warrant that cannot survive the neighbour-parity test plus an exclusivity claim with no sweep digit; no boundary change is proposed and none is needed.
rulings.remedy: Work order, fields boundary_rationale (primary) and device_notes (dependent). (1) In boundary_rationale, replace the fresh-figure differentiator with the byte-attested seam evidence: splice the verse-final speech attribution from oshb:Jer.48.8, cite it at byte tier with its digit (sweep: 1 verse), keep the imperative onset at oshb:Jer.48.9 as the far-side signal, and state explicitly that no such closing attribution precedes oshb:Jer.48.6. TEST THAT KILLED THE ORIGINAL: the rewritten warrant, applied verbatim at oshb:Jer.48.6, must NOT generate a seam there; any wording that would equally license a cut at oshb:Jer.48.6 fails. (2) In boundary_rationale, either give the singleness sentence an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit (token-bound: 1 verse; bare consonantal substring: 118 verses, 132 token occurrences) or delete the singleness wording; TEST: the exclusivity sentence must carry a digit naming the swept object and its unit in the same sentence, and a byte-tier label does not substitute. (3) Leave the two self-scoped statements in boundary_rationale and device_notes as written - they are false positives. No span change is ordered or proposed: the boundary stands on the evidence above; any respan would be a proposal requiring adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both challenges, one and the same defect: the row calls Jer.48.20 the second of the book's twelve doubled ketiv/qere verses, when in that book-ordered inventory it stands eighth (Jer.48.7 being seventh); the cure is to drop the ordinal.
rulings.grounds: Both challenges raise one and the same defect, and it is upheld. Re-derived from the byte-derived mark inventory rather than from either challenge's list: the verses carrying more than one variant note, in book order, are Jer.3.19, Jer.4.19, Jer.6.25, Jer.13.20, Jer.14.14, Jer.22.23, Jer.48.7, Jer.48.20, Jer.49.39, Jer.50.6, Jer.50.11 and Jer.51.34 (12 verses, inside a book-wide layer of 141 notes over 124 verses, single-witness). oshb:Jer.48.20 is the EIGHTH member and carries exactly two notes; oshb:Jer.48.7 is the seventh. The row's sentence scopes the set to the book, so no chapter-scoped reading rescues the ordinal: within ch 48 the site would be second, but that is not what the field says, and the scope is stated there explicitly. Object check, not digit check: the challenges' count object (multi-note verses, book order) is the right object and their digit holds, so this is a true ordinal error against the campaign's largest disclosure inventory rather than a reproduced digit attached to the wrong object. Everything else the row discloses for its span verifies independently and completely: one variant note at oshb:Jer.48.18 and two at oshb:Jer.48.20, each given written-against-read in the correct direction; one paseq seg at oshb:Jer.48.20 cited count-only with no intra-verse position (single-witness, seg layer); and no parashah mark and no further paseq seg anywhere in oshb:Jer.48.17-Jer.48.20 (0 marks, 1 seg in the span), with none claimed. Severity medium: a digit-class error in the heaviest disclosure layer, curable in one sentence with no consequence for the span.
rulings.remedy: Work order, field boundary_rationale. Delete 'the second of' from the doubled-note sentence and state membership in the twelve without an ordinal, exactly as the same disclosure is made at oshb:Jer.48.7; if an ordinal is wanted, write the book-order position (eighth of twelve) or name the chapter scope explicitly with its own digit. Leave both written-against-read pairs and the paseq disclosure as they stand - both verify. TEST THAT KILLED THE ORIGINAL: any ordinal in a mark-disclosure claim must resolve against the book-order list of multi-note verses (3:19, 4:19, 6:25, 13:20, 14:14, 22:23, 48:7, 48:20, 49:39, 50:6, 50:11, 51:34); a scope-less ordinal fails by default.

rulings.challenge_claim: Three items on one row: the closing form contrast leans on translation-layer poetry-line metadata, states that metadata inaccurately, and names the staged data key verbatim in prose; and the rationale's statement that no fresh tier-1 onset follows at Jer.48.26 conflicts with the imperative-onset warrant used at Jer.48.9, understating the row's own closing warrant.
rulings.grounds: All three items are real; the third one's framing needs correcting, and that correction explains why the same row can be read as sound or as defective depending on which field is read. Item 1, the line-count texture: upheld on its policy ground. Modern poetry-line breaks are translation-layer metadata that is never boundary evidence and never counterevidence, so it cannot do the distinguishing work device_notes assigns it (texture distinguishing this span from the scene before it and the scene after it). The figures also fail to support the wording: in the staged folded text the in-span counts run 1, 0, 0, 1, 1 across web:Jer.48.21-Jer.48.25 against 3, 4, 2, 3 across web:Jer.48.17-Jer.48.20 and 3 at web:Jer.48.26 - a relative contrast in which three of the five in-span verses carry a line, not a run at or near zero. Independently re-derived; the challenge's digits are exact. Item 2, the leaked key: real, with its class corrected - what surfaces in device_notes is a staged data FIELD name, machine register inside row prose, rather than a staged file name or stem; the cure is identical either way. Item 3, the onset misclassification: real, and its locus is sharper than the challenge states. NEW FINDING: the conflict is not primarily with the neighbouring seam at Jer.48.9 - it is INSIDE this row. boundary_rationale calls oshb:Jer.48.26 'a fresh imperative with a different figure' and, in the same sentence, says the row stops there 'since no fresh tier-1 onset follows immediately at that verse'; strongest_rejected_alternative says the opposite, that the form 'shifts cleanly' into 'a fresh imperative scene with its own figure at the very next verse' and uses it as one of two independent grounds. Both statements quote the row correctly, so the row supports opposite readings of its own closing warrant field by field. The bytes settle it: oshb:Jer.48.26 opens הַשְׁכִּירֻ֕הוּ (byte), a plural imperative with object suffix and Moab in the third person - the same device class the unit beginning at that verse carries as its onset driver and the same class used as the onset driver at oshb:Jer.48.9 - while oshb:Jer.48.25 closes verse-final on נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.25, byte; the last two of the verse's seven tokens). Under the ruled ordering the closing formula therefore DOES count as corroboration, so the row's own prose understates a warrant the bytes grant it. Severity held at low: the boundary is not in question. The list form at the onset is byte-true (the names are chained by repeated conjunctions with no verbal frame between them across oshb:Jer.48.22-Jer.48.24), the closing formula is verse-final, a fresh onset follows, and the span's mark disclosure verifies complete (one variant note at oshb:Jer.48.21; no paseq seg and no parashah mark anywhere in oshb:Jer.48.21-Jer.48.25 (0 marks, 0 segs), none claimed). All three items are prose repairs with no span consequence.
rulings.remedy: Work order, two fields. (a) device_notes: delete the clause carrying the machine line-count field name and its at-or-near-zero characterization; if a form contrast is kept, ground it only in the byte-attested chain of repeated conjunctions across oshb:Jer.48.22-Jer.48.24. TEST: no translation-layer line or paragraph datum may appear in any field as a distinguishing or corroborating signal in either direction, and no staged data field name may appear in row prose. (b) boundary_rationale: replace 'no fresh tier-1 onset follows immediately at that verse' with the byte-true statement that a plural-imperative onset does stand at oshb:Jer.48.26 (splice the onset token, byte tier), so the verse-final formula at oshb:Jer.48.25 is closure corroboration under the ruled ordering, and align the sentence with strongest_rejected_alternative, which already carries the two-ground reading. TEST THAT KILLED THE ORIGINAL: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative must be read together and must not assert opposite things about the same verse; any closure claim must name the following verse's onset device class with its byte citation. Consolidation note, no per-row action: the plural imperative without a named vocative is treated as a seam driver at Jer.48.9 and Jer.48.26 and denied at Jer.48.6 and inside this row's own rationale at Jer.48.26 - one consistent treatment of that class across the Moab stretch is a sweep-shaped order, not a single-row edit.
